newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia says Briton captive escaped Khmer Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia says Briton captive escaped Khmer Rouge.

text.p: A Cambodian military official said on Thursday that British mine clearance expert Christopher Howes, believed to have been kidnapped by the Khmer Rouge in late March, had escaped.

"He escaped, I don't know when," Major-General Tom Sambol told Reuters. He said Armed Forces Deputy Chief of Staff Lieutenant-General Nhiek Bun Chhay had gone to northern Cambodia to bring Howes to Phnom Penh.
A representative from the British-based Mines Advisory Group, the organisation Howes worked for, said he had heard a rumour that Howes had been released but had no further details.
There have been mixed reports over the past few months about the fate of Howes and his interpreter Houn Hourth. Both were abducted in the northwest province of Siem Reap in March.

In August the Bangkok Post said Howes had been executed in the Maoist group's Anlong Veng stronghold and Houn Hourth died of malaria in July. But a breakaway Khmer Rouge commander said in October that Howes was still alive in captivity. Earlier this week Khmer Rouge hardliners denied holding Howes.

Tom Sambol said he heard Howes had escaped to Staung, near Kompong Thom, about 120 km (72 miles) north of Phnom Penh. He said Nhiek Bun Chhay had travelled to Kompong Thom to pick up Howes but did not say anything about Houn Hourth.
